input_facts.text:
An EIA article published April 27, 2020 reports that May-delivery WTI futures traded as low as minus $40.32 per barrel around 2:30 p.m. ET on April 20. June-delivery Brent closed at positive $19.33 per barrel on April 21; longer-dated WTI prices were also positive.
WTI contracts held through expiration require delivery arrangements at Cushing unless other arrangements were made in advance.
For April 17, the article reports 76 million barrels of working storage capacity and about 58 million barrels in tanks, with another roughly 2 million in transit. Physically unfilled capacity may already be leased or committed.

adjudication_excerpt.text: The negative observation is an intraday price for a specified WTI contract, not a quoted settlement or a universal oil price. The positive Brent comparison differs in benchmark, delivery month and day. Eighteen million barrels of arithmetic tank space does not establish that an unprepared trader could rent it. Physical emptiness and commercial availability differ. This April 27 retrospective cannot be represented as a proved April 20 decision-time input, and supplies no forecast or trade.

question_en: Compare the reported oil prices by instrument, time and price type; calculate the apparent tank space and assess its significance for a trader facing delivery, including the information-date limitation.
